score_notes.novelty: writing-mode:vertical-rl + WAAPI seamless-loop rain is a fresh mechanism for this catalogue, but the found-object pairs with the now-crowded source-vs-render DNA (Silencio, Non-finito, Rivers, La Disparition) so the pairing has been seen.
score_notes.nuance: the toggle that returns the layout engine to flat prose is a near-perfect wall-text-killer for the literate reading, and the five-selectable / echo-non-selectable split is precise, but the footer footnote partially explains what the toggle should carry alone.
score_notes.narrative: explicitly inherits from the source-vs-render line (Silencio, Indivisible, Rivers, Non-finito) and articulates order (vertical-rl) vs chance (per-visit speed/phase/line choice) cleanly, yet does not introduce a new move the twenty-year argument lacked.
score_notes.craft: one HTML file, a clean even-units seamless loop, modest per-visit randomisation; the echoed non-selectable fills and resize rebuild add minor machinery beyond the smallest build that completes the thought.
score_notes.wit: the rain is the surface gag and the toggle revealing five plain sentences is the second landing on re-read; the footnote line 'it was only ever a sentence' carries the cheerful-cynic tone well.

references_named: Stéphane Mallarmé, Un Coup de Dés (1897)
Eugen Gomringer / Augusto de Campos (concrete poetry)
rationale: Solidly inside the catalogue's source-vs-render line: Apollinaire's 1918 calligrammatic gesture is enacted literally by CSS writing-mode:vertical-rl plus a seamless Web Animations API translation loop, so the layout engine becomes the weather (P1, P4). The stop-the-rain toggle returning the engine to horizontal-tb and exposing five plain prose sentences is a well-built double-reading moment, the five-selectable / echo-non-selectable split keeps the clipboard honest, and the viewport-height measure echoes the measurement tradition. The mechanism is genuinely fresh to this catalogue, but the broader source-vs-render pairing is well-rehearsed.
reservations: The catalogue now has many source-vs-render works (Silencio, La Disparition, Non-finito, Rivers, Indivisible, Rubrica, Scrittura Speculare, Schreibzeit, Un Coup de Dés, Window Sign); this is a competent fresh instantiation but does not extend the argument's grammar with a new move. The footer footnote is mildly explanatory where the toggle already carries the literate reading on its own.
revision_suggestion: Push the chance further so each reload yields a structurally different rain (which sentences appear, in what order, with what rhythm), and strip or compress the footer so the toggle alone delivers the double-reading — reducing the explanatory residue and sharpening the work's place against its source-vs-render siblings.
